items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Because they wanted you to do Bach or Beethoven or somebody like that?

ctx.x: Yes. They didn’t blame me, they could have, he got in trouble. And I said that’s it. Let me out of here. I’ll never take another music course in the school system. And that probably plants the seed of preventing me from overcoming my inferiority, which was for the best, but I was doing off on my own, and I guess I would be fifteen, and intentionally curtailing the music program in the New York City public school system for a righteous, accurate and correct reason. I was mad as hell. Still am obviously.
Because they wanted you to do Bach or Beethoven or somebody like that?

Yeah it was inappropriate. The teacher had approved the topic so it was him who got into trouble, not me, the grade stood. But I said I’ll never take another music course. And that was besides — two more years, two and a half. And I never did. And I was mad. And they wouldn’t let me talk about Duke Ellington in the classroom either. That continued at Columbia. So I said later for the music major at Columbia, the American history department was hiring me to teach jazz in their American history seminars. I said oh…
